title: Rat Model of Adhesive Capsulitis of the Shoulder
protocol: Induce anesthesia in the rat with 5% isoflurane through inhalation in an induction chamber.
Sustain anesthesia during surgery with 2% isoflurane through a nose cone.
Maintain body temperature using a water-based heating element underneath the animal.
Administer sustained-release buprenorphine subcutaneously at a dose of 1.2 mg/kg depending on the rat’s body weight for pain control.
Measure baseline torque as a function of rotation angle between 60° of external rotation and 80° of internal rotation before surgical immobilization.
Immobilize the left glenohumeral joints at an angle of 60° of abduction.
Start the surgical procedure with a posterior longitudinal incision, parallel to the humeral shaft.
Make the skin incision just below the glenohumeral joint and extend for about 3 cm.
Use 2 sutures (braided polyester) to immobilize the glenohumeral joint by piercing through the lateral edge of the scapula and around the distal two thirds of the humeral shaft.
Tighten the sutures carefully to avoid constricting critical structures such as the brachial artery.
Achieve an approximation of the scapular blade plane by maintaining the arm at 60° of abduction when considering the Z plane, while allowing free movement in X and Y planes.
Ensure proper hemostasis before closing the skin incision using skin clips.
Close the skin incision with skin clips after ensuring proper hemostasis.
Discontinue anesthesia and allow the animal to recover under supervision in a warm environment.
Return the animal to its cage once it regains sufficient consciousness to maintain sternal recumbency.
Inspect the incision sites daily during the first post-operative week.
Remove wound clips on the 10th day after surgery.
Administer sustained-release buprenorphine subcutaneously at a dose of 1.2 mg/kg starting at anesthesia induction.
Repeat administration of sustained-release buprenorphine every 72 hours if needed.
Induce anesthesia with 5% isoflurane through inhalation in an induction chamber.
Sustain anesthesia with 2% isoflurane through a nose cone throughout the surgery.
Make an incision on top of the scar from the previous procedure.
Cut the sutures and remove them from the humerus and the scapula.
Close the incision with wound clips.
Examine the incision site daily during the first week to detect any signs of infection.
Monitor pain and distress.
Measure ROM and passive shoulder mechanics before and after immobilization using a customized device.
Perform measurements pre-operatively (baseline) and continuously after suture removal.
Measure ROM immediately after suture removal (follow-up day 0).
Measure ROM subsequently twice a week.
Reduce measurement frequency to once weekly upon recording less than 10% change from the previous time point.
Use a customized device consisting of an arm clamp, sensor assembly, and pivoting axle for measurements.
Carry out measurements under anesthesia using isoflurane via precision vaporizer at 5% for induction.
Maintain anesthesia with isoflurane at 2% during the full procedure (approximately 5 minutes).
Use a water-based heating element underneath the animal to maintain body temperature during anesthesia.
Position the animal properly for ROM measurement with the aid of a laser guide.
Place the forelimb on the arm clamp in 90° forward flexion, aligning the sensing axis with the long axis of the humerus.
Secure the forelimb by the wrist and elbow as illustrated.
Control passive forelimb rotation by a stepper motor to assess ROM and torque consistently.
Control the stepper motor using a microcontroller.
Connect inputs from an inclinometer and a torque sensor to indicate measurement start and end points.
Connect the microcontroller to a computer for control via in-house developed MATLAB code.
Cycle the sensor assembly 3 times between 60° external rotation and 80° internal rotation for baseline measurements.
Use initial torque measurements (external: text, internal: tint) for comparison.
For ROM measurements, use each animal's baseline torque values as preset variables to detect changes in rotation ROM.
Detect changes with a resolution of 0.2°.
For stiffness measurements, use original angles of 60° external and 80° internal rotations as preset variables to detect changes in torque.
Detect changes with a resolution of 0.01 Nmm.
Weigh animals on the same day as each ROM assessment.
Place animals on scales and record their masses.
Return rats to their cages following recovery.
Monitor rats for signs of pain or distress.
Euthanize rats with CO2 exposure at the end of the study period.
Dissect both left (immobilized) and right (healthy control) shoulders.
Fix excised shoulders in a solution of 10% neutral buffered formalin for 3 days.
Decalcify fixed shoulders in EDTA 10% at pH 7.4 for 2 months.
Mix samples on a shaker in a gentle agitation cycle.
Store samples at 4 °C during the process.
Monitor decalcification of the glenohumeral joint with weekly microcomputed tomography (uCT) scans.
Replace decalcification fluid at least 3 to 4 times per week.
Mount the glenohumeral joints in paraffin stacks for histological sectioning.
Orient the samples to allow for coronal slices.

Perform antigen retrieval by microwave irradiation by submerging the slides in a plastic Coplin jar containing sodium citrate buffer solution (10 mM sodium citrate, 0.05% Tween 20, pH 6.0) and placing in a regular microwave oven for 10 minutes at medium power.
Allow slides to cool for 30 min at room temperature.
Perform blocking with goat serum for 30 min.
Incubate the specimens with a primary mouse monoclonal antibody (1:400 dilution) to fibronectin overnight at 4 °C.
Wash specimens twice with PBS (0.5 ug/mL) for 10 minutes after incubation with the primary antibody.
Incubate with a secondary antibody, goat antimouse IgG-peroxidase conjugate (1:400 dilution), for 30 minutes.
Wash the specimens twice with PBS (2.5 µg/mL) on a shaker for 10 minutes.
Expose to 3,30-diaminobenzidine tetrahydrochloride and 30% hydrogen peroxide in the dark for 10 min.
Counterstain with Carazzi hematoxylin.
